title: The unions of Abba and Ima: Shabbos, Yom Tov and the week of the mind, up to the birth of souls
overview:
The last chapter showed three ways *chachma* and *bina* receive from the *Keser*: from the *mazalos*, where a person loves a thing for itself and so sees every detail; from the *zro'os*, where the intellect is the emotions' puppet; and from *Nehi*, where it is a tool for a goal it cannot question. This chapter shows the same range in *Abba* and *Ima* themselves.

Their inner union is *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov*, leisure for the mind. On *Shabbos* *chachma* rests and sees G-dliness as it is, before it is named; on *Yom Tov* *bina* enjoys the inner point, through symbols and *mitzvos*. Their outer side, the *middos* of the intellect, is the mind that leans to a verdict: felt without reasons in *Yisroel Saba*, like Rav who kept silent, and explained in *Tevuna*; and its *Nehi* weighs how to carry the verdict out, with conviction or without. The inner union is like a couple who simply enjoy each other; in the *Shema* it is reached by *mesirus nefesh*. Souls are born only from a union that reaches the *mazalos*, as only a great sage who knows an idea at its source can teach it to a child.

sections.title: The light goes down through Abba and Ima themselves: from the mazalos to the outer Nehi
sections.summary: Chapter 25 explained the ways *chachma* and *bina* receive from the *Keser*: from the *mazalos*, from the *zro'os*, or from *Nehi*. This chapter shows the whole range of *Abba* and *Ima* themselves, from their inner intellect that receives from *Arich* to their outer *Nehi* that goes into *Zeir Anpin*; and the level they receive from decides how true the intellect is.

blocks.text: The last chapter: *Chabad* (*chachma*, *bina* and *daas*) receives from the *Keser* (crown) in three ways. From the *mazalos* (lit. the flows; he compares them to hairs), which reach up to its essence; from the *zro'os* (the arms), the *middos* (emotional attributes) of the *Keser*; or normally, from the *Nehi* (*netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*) of *Arich Anpin*, as the *Nehi* of the higher goes into the lower.

blocks.text: This chapter explains three levels of the *yichud* (union) of *Abba* and *Ima*: *chachma* and *bina* as *partzufim* (statures) working together on an idea. They are *trein rei'in d'lo misparshin*, two companions that never part. An idea in *chachma* is at once analyzed, ordered and named in *bina*, and analysis in *bina* looks to *chachma* for how it all fits together.

blocks.text: Rabbi Walters offers a reading of his own: the three levels of the union match the three sources of the last chapter, each union on the level it receives from. The middle one, from the *zro'os*, is intellect blinded by emotion, "like a puppet"; above it is the union that gets from the *mazalos*.

blocks.text: A review of the last chapter. When a person desires the intellect itself, it comes from the *Chabad* of the *ratzon* (will), and he pursues the true idea. From the emotions, the intellect is a puppet that justifies them. From *Nehi* it is a tool, a *merkava* (a vehicle for the will): objective, but only about the means, since the goal is not up for discussion. That is everyday intellect: at your job you do not ask whether it is the right job for you, only how to do it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: On *Shabbos* you are meant to be on the level of the *mazalos*. Intellect from them carries the hidden inner *taanug* (delight) and makes a person very smart. The *mazalos* belong to the *mocha stima'a* (the hidden brain) of *Arich Anpin*, but their root is higher, in the liquid of the brain and the skull: the *middos* of *Atik* enclothed in *Arich*. So *pnimiyus Abba* (the inner side of *Abba*) is *pnimiyus Atik*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: So a person with a big talent for something has an intellect that receives from the *mazalos* in it: he loves the thing as an end in itself, and his intellect enjoys every detail. The more a thing is a means to an end, the less you care and the more superficially you look, passing over the details that would make you really good at it.

blocks.text: That is why someone like the Rebbe is very smart at everything, even naturally, and why *Chassidus* taken to heart makes us smart too: what makes a person stupid is passing over the details, looking at things generally, as a *girsa* (rote) thing.

blocks.title: The kid with the hockey cards
blocks.text:
Most things a person thinks unimportant, so he does not think about them. His teacher told of a kid who was weak at math and at school in general, but knew every statistic of every player on his hockey cards and could work out all the percentages, "because he loved it."

A person who enjoys only the football goes through everything else on autopilot, doing the bare minimum and missing the details.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: *Chassidus* teaches you to find the G-dliness in everything; that is *iyun* (close analysis). The *iyun* and *girsa* of the first chapter are really about how you go through the world: whether you stop to find the *Elokus* (G-dliness) in things or pass over it. When everything has *Elokus*, each thing is an end in itself; you care about its details and spend time on it, and that makes you good at everything, especially when you see how they connect.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: That is the *mazalos*: your essential *taanug* goes into the thing, so you want the thing itself. They are like hairs because a hair's *tzimtzum* (contraction) brings the whole essence over "in a tiny drop." So you see each thing as *mamash* (actually) G-dliness, a *metzumtzam* (contracted) piece of the real goal and not a means to it, and that makes a bigger intellect with a bigger *taanug* in it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 30 reads no line of the chapter: it is his introduction to the whole chapter, placed under its first line.

blocks.text: If it is only the *zro'os*, the *middos* going into *chachma* and *bina*, he is like a very smart person who thinks into everything he sees, but with an agenda: he uses everything to prove his view.

blocks.title: Proving the Rebbe is Moshiach
blocks.text:
Say somebody is always trying to prove that the Rebbe is *Moshiach*. That is how he learns a *sicha* (talk), and really how he does everything: he does not value the thing itself or its lesson, only uses it for his point.

He can use it as the puppet or as a means to an end. As a means to an end, he learns publishing and radio to spread his belief, but he does not really care about them at all.

blocks.title: Parents who overlook what their child did
blocks.text: So he feels threatened and has to twist it. Parents who love their child see him do something wrong, and their intellect often twists it to overlook it; a person does the same with himself when something he did contradicts how he sees himself. That he, or his child, is good is already a given, and this threatens it. That is the level of the *middos*: the thing is not the essence but a symptom of it.

blocks.title: Driving to work
blocks.text:
There the thing must fit the essential thing, and whatever does not is a threat. *Nehi* is not threatening: working out how to drive to work, you do not mind a detour; you just want to get there and get the money.

The decision to go to work at all is a bias of love: you have to provide for your family. How to get there is cold; providing for them is hot. It is not the love itself, since you could love them without going to work, but a sign of it: to love them and not want to provide for them "doesn't look great."

blocks.text: Now: **now we have to understand the way the light goes down further, how it goes through the ten sefiros of Abba and Ima themselves**. The *mashal* (analogy) of *Abba* and *Ima* is a father and a mother.

This applies wherever the *Keser* goes into *chachma* and *bina*, but it is discussed *davka* (specifically) in *Atzilus*, because that is where the *partzufim* (*Atik*, *Arich*, *Abba*, *Ima*, *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, five or six however you count them) are spoken of. Above *Atzilus*, before the *Tikun* (the world of Repair), lights are not divided into vessels, so there is no *partzuf*, only the points of *Tohu*; the *Adam* of *Adam Kadmon* is a general *partzuf* for everything.

And they are not in *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, because there the *partzuf* is not real: it is only revealed in something separate. Those worlds are like thought, speech and action, separate from the essence.

blocks.title: The student in class and at recess
blocks.text: A *partzuf* is a person's ten powers used for one thing. Using all ten to learn is *Abba*, a learning personality. The same student in class and at recess can be totally different. His hobbies and what he enjoys are an *Atik*-*Arich* *partzuf*; what you normally call his personality, whether he is a nice guy, is his *Zeir Anpin*; how good he is at speaking and doing, whether he is a charismatic speaker, is a *Nukva*. These are the conscious mind revealed in the body.

That is *Atzilus*: consciousness as it is revealed in the body. Above it is the subconscious. Below it the *partzufim* come out into what you say or do, "but it's not alive anymore." So plain *partzufim* belong to *Atzilus*, the world of *Tikun*, which is why chapter seven, at the start of the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), puts them there; elsewhere they apply differently.

Earlier or later it would not fit, since there it is not what that level stresses. The light that goes down is the revelation of the person's self: how it comes down and stays transparent through the ten *sefiros* of *Abba*, the intellect.

blocks.text: **From the level of the pnimiyus of the intellect of chachma and bina**: the inner side of the *mochin* (lit. brains, the intellect) receives from **chesed and gevura of Arich Anpin**, and more inner still, **when they receive from the mazalos of Arich Anpin**. That is rare; normal intellect is the emotions and the *Nehi*, and most people barely tap into the *mazalos*.

Most people, even doing philosophy, are on the level of the *middos*: not pursuing the truth so much as emotionally defending their world view, which is why they get emotional about it. They feel the conclusions threaten how they live, or their view of themselves as good; that they come at it to reach a conclusion at all shows they are on that level.

*Chassidus* does not tell you good or bad about anything. It tells you clearly what each thing is and how everything fits together, which lets you find the good in everything in a detached way. "The real question is when to use which one, not which one is true."

Then there are people with a real *chush* (sense) for something, geniuses passionately into it, enjoying every little detail like a real artist. That is a *mazalos* guy: the thing, with its details, is an end in itself. To be like that in philosophy he has to love truth, understanding the way things are, as a *lishma* thing, like pure science; even applying it, he does it to see how it is applied, not as a means to an end.
The real *mazalos* thing is *Chassidus*. Even the other levels of Torah are not really like the *mazalos*, which is why they are *halacha* (law) and such things.

blocks.text: So the range runs from the *mazalos* **all the way down to when only the external Nehi of Abba and Ima**, enclothed in the *mochin* of *Zeir Anpin*, give, as in *Etz Chaim*: the whole spectrum of *Abba* and *Ima*. The last chapter was the ways the *Keser* gives to *Abba* and *Ima*; this one is the levels of *Abba* and *Ima* themselves, from receiving from the *mazalos* down to giving into *Zeir Anpin*.

sections.title: Shabbos and Yom Tov: the inner union of chachma and bina, for its own sake
sections.summary: The inner *mochin* of *Abba* and *Ima* are like *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov*, leisure for the mind. *Shabbos* is called *kodesh* and *oneg*: *chachma* resting, seeing G-dliness as it is, as an end in itself; *Yom Tov* is only *mikra kodesh* and *simcha*: *bina* enjoying the inner point of the idea, through symbols and *mitzvos*. Where the two meet, *havein b'chachma v'chacham b'vina*, is the inner union of *Abba* and *Ima*.

blocks.text: **And the inyan is known, that it's like Shabbos and Yom Tov.** They are a *mashal* (analogy) for the inner intellect of *Abba*, **because Shabbos is called holy**, *kodesh*, and *chachma milsa b'garmei*: **chachma is a thing onto its own**. *Kodesh* means removed from everything else and needing nothing, the pleasure in it itself; so *Shabbos* is *kodesh b'oneg*, holy in delight.

*Shabbos* is when you rest your *chachma*. Work and leisure differ less in what you do than in whether you want to do it: leisure you enjoy as an end in itself and would do even without the money; work you would rather not do, but you need the money.

*Shabbos* and *Yom Tov* are leisure: on *Shabbos* your *chachma* rests and has fun, on *Yom Tov* your *bina*. *Shabbos* is the inner side of *chachma*, an end in itself; using *chachma* to figure out right, wrong and how to act is its outer side, for the week.

On *Shabbos* your *chachma*, your creative ability, gets a break from making money, and even from figuring out *halachos*, to do what it likes: see G-dliness in things purely, like pure science. Applications are work for it.

During the week things are bad and you have to be *mevarer* them (sort them out): *b'chachma isbariru*, with *chachma* you sort out how to act. Then nothing is really G-dliness: you would rather learn *Chassidus* in yeshiva, and you have to learn law, do business, even eat and sleep. Most days are a drag. *Shabbos* is a whole different *hisbonenus* (contemplation).

On *Shabbos* you look for the actual G-dliness in everything, *b'chol derachecha da'eihu* (know Him in all your ways). Nothing needs fixing: G-d made it, so it holds His wisdom. That is why on *Shabbos* you enjoy the taste of food, not only its energy as in the week: how He chose to make it taste reveals His wisdom too, and it is a *mitzva* (commandment) to enjoy it.

blocks.title: Playing the game and watching the video
blocks.text:
During the week the *mitzva* is to be *mevarer* the world. In a basketball game you do not say it is just a game: you care, try hard, and give the other guy no free shot because he messed up, or you ruin the game. Afterwards, watching the video, you enjoy even your own mess-ups, without being a sore sport.

G-d has both. Six days you play the game. On *Shabbos* you rest and enjoy the beauty, like a vacation, and even your *hisbonenus* is not sorting out your *middos* but appreciating that everything is *Elokus*.

blocks.text: **This is the pnimiyus of the or Abba**, the inner side of the light of *chachma*: the pleasure of thinking about something you really enjoy, here G-dliness. A person is revealed mainly when he uses his *chachma* in something he loves. That is the inner side of its light, from the *mazalos*, and it shows what he enjoys; outer *chachma* shows only the *chachma*, not what he is choosing.

That is the difference between the *mitzvos* and the world. The world is like outer *chachma*: you see G-d's wisdom, how He chose to make it, but not what He chose to represent Himself and connect Himself to. That is the *mitzvos*.

The inner side of *Abba* is the inner side of *Atik*: **so that's the pnimiyus of Atik Yomin**, the inner pleasure. So *v'karasa laShabbos oneg*, **you should call Shabbos pleasure, or that you should bring pleasure into Shabbos**, because the *taanug* is revealed in the *chachma*. **As explained elsewhere at length about the three seudos** (meals) **of Shabbos**, for *Chakal Tapuchin Kadishin* (the field of holy apples), *Atik Yomin* and *Zeir Anpin*; how they connect, he says, he does not know much.

blocks.text: **And Yom Tov is called not kodesh, it's only called mikra kodesh** (a calling of holiness), a lower level. On *Shabbos* the *chachma* goes up; on *Yom Tov* only the *bina*, while the *chachma* still works. So on *Yom Tov* you may do *borer* (sorting) for *ochel nefesh* (preparing food), and on *Shabbos* not.

*Yom Tov* is analyzing the world to understand it in human intellect, not seeing G-dliness in its purest state. That brings the idea down: you take things from the world to compare, make *meshalim* (analogies), order it, see it in examples. That is *ochel nefesh*: you make food from the world "to feed the G-dliness," seeing it indirectly, come down from its essential state. That is *bina*.

*Yom Tov* also has a *chumra* (stringency) over *Shabbos*: *nolad* (a thing newly come into being) is *muktza* (not to be handled) on *Yom Tov* and not on *Shabbos*. *Yom Tov* analyzes what you already have; dealing with new information, *chiddushim* (new insights), is work for *bina*. *Shabbos* is *chachma*, whose essence is coming up with new things.

*Yom Tov* is a lot more fun than *Shabbos*, but less restful: you can carry your *sefarim* and make food, so it is easier to party. On *Shabbos* you cannot do anything, so you worry about nothing, not even making food: "The way it is, that's the way it is, and you just enjoy it."

*Yom Tov* is *mikra kodesh*, **which is simcha** (joy). *Oneg* (delight) reveals *kodesh* directly, so *Shabbos* is called *oneg*; *Yom Tov* is its spreading into your *yeshus* (sense of self), which is *simcha*. As chapter four said, *chachma* makes *bittul* (self-nullification) and *bina* makes *simcha*. In *chachma* you lose your *metzius* (existence) and feel the thing; in *simcha* you understand it in your own vessels and have it, "you're the boss," and since it is very big, the joy is big.

That is *mikra kodesh*, **like it says, the mother of the children rejoices**: *bina* associates a thing with something outside it. *Mikra* is calling, naming: you connect to the essence, but artificially. It is not yet applying it, which is the week; you find ways to represent it, so it is no longer the thing itself. That is human intellect: symbols, names and systems that represent the idea. So it is *mikra'ei kodesh*: called *kodesh*, not essentially *kodesh*.

So *Yom Tov* has *mitzvos* you have to do, and *Shabbos* none. On *Yom Tov* we express our connection to G-dliness; on *Shabbos* it is essential and needs nothing to show it. You do not even have to make *kiddush*: the *mitzva d'oraisa*, he thinks, is not to say it but to enjoy things, to have wine. The point is to appreciate that G-d made the world and rested, that everything has that G-dliness, and you say *kiddush* to be conscious of it, to be *mekadesh* the day. There are good food, nice clothes and a nice table, but no real *mitzvos* of the day.

On *Yom Tov* you have wine whether you enjoy it or not: no *simcha* without wine. Once it must come a certain way, you have set how to represent it, and "it's out of your hands a little bit already."

sensitivity.reason: Says as a rule that on Shabbos one who does not enjoy wine is not supposed to have wine, which a reader might take as a ruling on kiddush wine.

blocks.text: *Chachma* says, just be yourself, we accept you as you are. So with the world: the point of *Shabbos* is to stop trying to change things and enjoy the world as it is. G-d made it perfect; you have nothing to do. There are no rules, except not to spoil the fun by thinking about work: "That's the only rule here: you have to have fun."

On *Yom Tov* you have already decided to have fun with a certain game, and you play by its rules: we show our connection to G-d through *matza* and *sukka*. These are general *mitzvos* that show our essential connection and *emuna* (faith). *Matza*, flat and tasteless, shows the *emuna* and represents the *chachma*. The *sukka* shows that Torah and *mitzvos* are not an end in themselves but a temporary thing we see through: we just want to connect to G-d. The *Yamim Tovim* reconnect us to see the week's *mitzvos* as the intermediate between the *chachma* of *Shabbos* and the week, an expression of the *chachma*. That is *bina*.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת מוחין דאימא שמקבל מאבא,
phrases.en: which this is the *mochin* of *Ima*, the intellect of *bina*, which receives from *chachma*.

phrases.he: כי השביתה דשבת הוא בחכמה גם כן
phrases.en: the resting of *Shabbos* is in *chachma*,

phrases.he: דהיינו בפנימית אבא, בחינת כח מה אין דחכמה
phrases.en: which that is the inner part of *chachma*, the *koach MaH*, which is the *ayin* of *chachma*,

phrases.he: קודם שמתפשט ליש בהשגה דבינה
phrases.en: even before it comes into be understood in *bina*.

blocks.text: *Em habanim semeicha*, **which this is the mochin of Ima, the intellect of bina, which receives from chachma**. **The resting of Shabbos is in chachma**, in **the koach MaH** (the power of "what"), **which is the ayin of chachma**, its nothing, **even before it comes into be understood in bina**. On *Shabbos* it is revealed: you take things in as they are, before you interpret and name them.

blocks.title: Drawing on the Right Side of the Brain
blocks.text:
*Drawing on the Right Side of the Brain* is a very good book about drawing, and a very good book about *chachma* and *bina*. Its whole point is to put you into *chachma* mode, the secret of drawing: look at the thing exactly as it is, instead of naming its parts and drawing what you named.

Looking at a face, a person sees eyes, nose, mouth and glasses and draws a symbol for each, though from his angle they may look nothing like the symbols. So you train yourself to draw what you see, lines and shadows, lights and darks, without naming it. Most details have no names, so naming leaves them out, and it does not look right.

Seen without naming and categorizing, a thing stays whole. Naming picks what you consider important, which is why *Atik* is revealed in *bina*: what you care about shows in the distinctions you make. It is like the blot test: the *chachma* is an uninterpreted blob, and the interpretation comes from you; you find what you look for. That is how *bina* reveals the *Atik*, what a person really enjoys.

phrases.he: וכן בינה בבחינת פנימית,
phrases.en: and the same thing that on *Yom Tov*, which is the *pnimiyus* of *bina*,

phrases.he: הוא עומק נקודת המושג כו',
phrases.en: that's the *omek nekudas hamusag* of *bina*.

phrases.he: כידוע שיש אין חכמה בבינה ובינה בחכמה
phrases.en: that there is the *ayin* of *chachma* goes into *bina*, and the inner thing of *bina* is in *chachma*.

blocks.text: **And the same thing that on Yom Tov, which is the pnimiyus of bina**: **that's the omek nekudas hamusag** (the depth of the point of the concept) **of bina**. On *Yom Tov* you focus on the inner point of the idea, not its proofs, examples or applications; that is the rest of *bina*. So on *Yom Tov* we focus on the inner point of the *mitzvos* and of sorting out the world, the goal.

blocks.title: The object of the game
blocks.text: The object of the game: in *bina* it is to win, to get the most points; in *chachma* it is just to have fun, and *chachma* can have fun doing anything, winning or not. In *bina* fun takes a form: it is fun to win. So on *Yom Tov* you do not do much work, since it is not practice time, but you do some, because you still have to win the game.

It is known **that there is the ayin of chachma goes into bina, and the inner thing of bina is in chachma**: at their inner points they connect. Analyzing anything, you analyze the thing itself, so there is always *chachma* in it; getting the *chachma*, you notice details and interpret a little, to see how it differs from other things, so there is always *bina*. You cannot really have one without the other.

phrases.he: והיינו הבן בחכמה וחכם בבינה,
phrases.en: that in the *chachma* itself, you'll be able to find the ability to make the distinctions and then explain it, and from the explanations, you'll be able to get the inner point, which is the *chachma*.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת יחוד פנימית דאבא ואמא
phrases.en: That's the inner *yichud* of *Abba* and *Ima*, *chachma* and *bina*,

blocks.text: That is *havein b'chachma v'chacham b'vina* (understand with wisdom and be wise with understanding): **that in the chachma itself, you'll be able to find the ability to make the distinctions and then explain it, and from the explanations, you'll be able to get the inner point**. **That's the inner yichud of Abba and Ima**, working together only for the inner truth of an idea, from the *mazalos*.

blocks.title: Three levels of a marriage
blocks.text: The simple *mashal* is a father and a mother. A married couple relates on three general levels. One is spending time together because they enjoy it, for no other purpose: the inner union of *Abba* and *Ima*, their mental connection and enjoyment of each other. The man has to come down to recognize the *bina*, the woman the *chachma*, and the love shows in small symbolic things, "like flowers and little notes." It is for themselves, not like raising kids together, doing the taxes or taking out the garbage.

blocks.title: Stuck in traffic, and raising kids
blocks.text:
Those too can be done with *pnimiyus*, as a chance to spend time together: stuck in traffic, it is an opportunity to be together, and who cares; *Nehi* mode is the rush to get there.

In between is raising kids. There is a level where a couple connect higher than the kids, the inner side; the regular, middle thing is that the purpose of marriage is to make a family. Then there are work and taxes, the practical things of living together: not the purpose, a means to keep the house going.

sections.title: The outer flow: the middos of chachma and bina, intellect that leans
sections.summary: When *chachma* and *bina* flow outward into their *Chagas* and *Nehi*, the intellect is a means to an end. The *middos* of *chachma*, its *vav ketzavos*, are the mind applied to a case or leaning toward kindness or judgment; they shine into the *middos* of *bina*, which give them good reasons, before they are born as emotions of their own.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בחיצונית השפע דחכמה ובינה בחג''ת נה''י כו',
phrases.en: On the other hand, when the *chitzoniyus hashpaa* is going into *Chagas* and *Nehi*

phrases.he: כמו מדות שבחכמה
phrases.en: Like the *middos* of *chachma*

phrases.he: שנקרא בחינת ו׳ קצוות דאבא
phrases.en: which are called the six directions, the six dimensions of *Abba*

blocks.text: **On the other hand, when the chitzoniyus hashpaa** (the outer flow) **is going into Chagas** (*chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*) **and Nehi**, it is a means to an end: **like the middos of chachma, which are called the six directions, the six dimensions of Abba**, the *vav ketzavos*. That is *chachma* expressed in a particular form within time and space: circumstantial, not the thing itself.

blocks.title: The law and the case
blocks.text: You learn a *halacha* as an abstract law. An actual case comes within certain circumstances of time and space: that is the *vav*. Applying the law to the case is *chachma* going into its six directions. A precedent is the opposite: you extrapolate the *chachma* from the particular case.

phrases.he: כמו חסד שבחכמה,
phrases.en: Like *chesed sheb'chachma*,

phrases.he: דהיינו כח שכל המטה כלפי חסד
phrases.en: like that you can use the intellect to lean towards *chesed*,

phrases.he: או כח שכל אחר שמטה כלפי דין כו'
phrases.en: or you have another *koach* of the *sechel* to go towards *din*.

blocks.text: And *middos*: **like chesed sheb'chachma** (kindness within wisdom), **that you can use the intellect to lean towards chesed, or you have another koach** (power) **of the sechel** (intellect) **to go towards din** (judgment). So intellect can prove emotions. But its real work is to understand how things are; using the facts to prove your views is using it for your own benefit.

phrases.he: ומאירים בחסד וגבורה דבינה
phrases.en: And the *chachma* shines into the *bina*, so the *middos* of *chachma* shine into the *middos* of the *bina*,

phrases.he: דהוא בא בהשגה בטוב טעם בהסבר לזכות ולחוב
phrases.en: So, in *bina*, it becomes very well explained, good reasoning for whether for merit or for guilt.

phrases.he: ונקרא מדות שבשכל המושג,
phrases.en: These are called the *middos*, the emotions of the intellect, which is understood,

phrases.he: קודם שנולדו במהות בפני עצמן (כמו שיתבאר)
phrases.en: before the *middos* become actual their own thing, before they become just *middos* without intellect, which is *Zeir Anpin*, like we'll explain later

blocks.text: **And the chachma shines into the bina, so the middos of chachma shine into the middos of the bina**, which come up with explanations to make it sound rational: the point behind the *midda*, why he thinks a thing good or bad. A person may have such a point and not be able to explain it, because his *bina* is not so good. That does not make it untrue; some people are just better at arguing.

**So, in bina, it becomes very well explained, good reasoning for whether for merit or for guilt.** **These are called the middos, the emotions of the intellect, which is understood, before the middos become actual their own thing**, *middos* without intellect, which is *Zeir Anpin*, whose birth is explained later.

sections.title: Shatik Rav: silence is a fence for wisdom
sections.summary: When a person sees that a thing is so and cannot explain it, that is the *middos* of *chachma* before they shine into *bina*, like Rav who kept silent. Silence protects a *chachma* from being argued away, and it keeps the mind open to the source of all ideas, so that being quiet "gets you double".

phrases.he: וכאשר אינו מוצא טעם בהסבר השגה,
phrases.en: and when you do not find a reason, that you can't explain it,

phrases.he: ומכל מקום לא יוכל לומר בהיפוך
phrases.en: but you still can't say the opposite.

phrases.he: כי שכלו מטה כך,
phrases.en: because his intellect leans that way.

phrases.he: היינו בבחינת חסד וגבורה דאבא קודם שמאיר מאין ליש בבינה
phrases.en: That is the emotions of *chachma* before they shine into *bina*.

phrases.he: (כמו ענין שתיק רב כו')
phrases.en: like it says about *shatik Rav*,

blocks.text: **And when you do not find a reason, that you can't explain it, but you still can't say the opposite**: you see it is true but cannot explain it. Not everybody is good at explaining; a person just sees that something is wrong and cannot say why, **because his intellect leans that way.** **That is the emotions of chachma before they shine into bina**, **like it says about shatik Rav** (Rav was silent).

blocks.title: Rav was silent
blocks.text: The *Gemara* in *Beitza* about *nolad*, an egg laid on *Yom Tov*, says *shatik Rav*. Some distinction kept one *halacha* from being learned from the other, but he could not find it, so he was quiet: he neither retracted his ruling nor argued further, and another sage explained it. That is the *mashal* for *Yisroel Saba* (lit. Israel the elder), the *middos* of *chachma*.

phrases.he: (והשתיקה סייג לחכמה,
phrases.en: a fence for the wisdom

phrases.he: משתוקא בתרין,
phrases.en: being quiet gets you double.

phrases.he: מפני שעולה ביטול כח מ''ה דחכמה זה למקור המוציא כל השכלות,
phrases.en: this *bittul* of the *koach MaH* of *chachma*, where you just experience it as it is, without interpreting it, you're able to go to the source of all the intellect,

phrases.he: שנקרא חכמה סתימאה כנזכר לעיל,
ומוציא משם השכלה חדשה כו')
phrases.en: and you can get out a new idea

blocks.text: *Ushtika seyag l'chachma*: silence is a fence that protects the *chachma*. The simple meaning, in *Pirkei Avos*, is that if you sit and listen you learn a lot, and once you open your mouth you stop learning. But why call that **a fence for the wisdom**? A fence protects something you already have. So he explains it further: when you have a *chachma* and give no reason for it, that protects it. Once you give a reason, it is open to be argued with and disproven.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's advice for a debate on TV
blocks.text:
The Rebbe told, he thinks, Rabbi Hollander, asked to debate Judaism with a Reform rabbi on TV and unwilling to give him credence as a legitimate rabbi, to say first thing that he does not agree with his stance at all and does not recognize him as a rabbi: "Now, let's discuss the issues."

He starts from a premise that is axiomatic and not open for debate: you are not a legitimate rabbi, and this ideology has nothing to do with Judaism, though you are Jewish because you were born Jewish. He can try to prove it, but even if he fails, it is not up for debate. That is one way silence is a fence for wisdom.

blocks.text: Also, when you are trying to get an idea you are quiet: in the *chachma* you see the thing itself, and interpreting it disturbs that. You have to let it in as it is. That is why a person with a flash of an idea goes quiet.

*Mishtuka b'trei* (silence is worth two). In *halacha*, a person sometimes makes a claim and gets $100 where, had he kept quiet, he would have got $200, because his claim impairs his rights: opening his mouth got him one, quiet would have got him two. **Being quiet gets you double.**

Here it means that the *bittul*, the silence, gives you a better understanding. *Chassidus* interprets nothing; it understands things as they are, and that is the difference between G-dly and human intellect. With **this bittul of the koach MaH of chachma, where you just experience it as it is, without interpreting it**, you get it objectively, so **you're able to go to the source of all the intellect**, the hidden *chachma*, **and you can get out a new idea**, since you did not put it in a box. Attach it to a reason and you limit it: if the reason is disproven the whole thing looks bad, and a *chiddush* outside that context is hard.

sections.title: Netzach and hod of Abba: the scales of the mind and the strength of conviction
sections.summary: The *Nehi* of *Abba* is the scales of the intellect, the *kelayos yo'atzos* that weigh how a verdict should be carried out. *Netzach* and *hod* are the mind's legs: a person who is *takif b'daito* stands by his view, and one who is not falls easily from guilt to innocence. Only from the *Nehi* of *Abba* in the *Nehi* of *Ima* come the *mochin* of *Zeir Anpin*.

phrases.he: ובחינת נה''י דאבא, היינו בחינת מאזני השכל והחכמה, איך שיבא הדבר חכמה לידי השפעה בבחינת כליות יועצות כו'

blocks.text: *Nehi* of *Abba* is the scales of the intellect: how the *chachma* comes to be given over. Once the intellect has decided whether a thing is good or bad, you must work out how to apply it, as the sentence follows the verdict. *Chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura* are the verdict, still abstract; the scales weigh what to do about it.

That is the *kelayos yo'atzos*, the kidneys that give advice. In doing it, should you go at it gung-ho, or timidly, with restraint? *Netzach* wants the full thing, good or bad, the full extent of the law. *Hod* holds back a little, because that would be better, or for fear it will be too much.

blocks.title: The lashes and the first offender
blocks.text:
Deciding how many lashes to give a man, *netzach* wants to give him all of them; *hod* is scared you will kill him. The purpose is that he live and be better, so you take care not to give too much and ruin his chance.

So a court often does not jail a first offender, especially a young one: they want him reformed, not rotting away there. If he keeps at it, "they throw the book at him."

phrases.he: (והיינו ענין התוקף שיש במוח, שנקרא תקיף בדעתו
phrases.en: This is also the force of your views, when you are strong-minded, when you're strong in your opinions, in your views.

phrases.he: כמו הרגלים
phrases.en: like the legs

phrases.he: שיש בהן כח להקים כל הגוף,
phrases.en: they have the strength to hold up the whole body.

phrases.he: כך בחינת נצח והוד דאבא מקימין לגוף המוחין
phrases.en: so too *netzach* and *hod* of the *chachma* hold up the actual intellect.

phrases.he: ולהיפוך
phrases.en: and the opposite,

phrases.he: כשאינו תקיף בדעתו,
phrases.en: a person is not strong-minded,

phrases.he: בקל יפול מסברתו מחוב לזכות
phrases.en: he can easily fall from his reasoning from guilt to innocence,

phrases.he: ומטמא לטהור כו'
phrases.en: impure to pure,

phrases.he: וכן בנצח והוד דאמא)
phrases.en: and the same thing with the *netzach* and *hod* of *Ima*.

blocks.text: This is *takif b'daito* (firm in his mind): **the force of your views, when you are strong-minded**. **Like the legs, they have the strength to hold up the whole body, so too netzach and hod of the chachma hold up the actual intellect.** Otherwise **he can easily fall from his reasoning from guilt to innocence**; **and the same thing with the netzach and hod of Ima**.
Without a strong *netzach* and *hod*, even though they are only the outer side of the intellect, you will not have the guts to seal it one way, because you can always argue the other side.

That is liberalism, or pluralism: they lack the strength in their view, the conviction, to stand up (the *mashal* of the legs) for what they believe in, take a stance and say, "That's it, this is it, and you are wrong."

sensitivity.reason: Names liberalism and pluralism as views whose holders lack conviction, a political jab.
sensitivity.publishable: That is a person who lacks the strength in his view, the conviction, to stand up (the *mashal* of the legs) for what he believes in, take a stance and say, "That's it, this is it, and you are wrong."

blocks.text: To have a legal system at all, you have to feel strongly enough that this is right and that is wrong to take responsibility for punishing someone, and that strength comes mainly from *netzach* and *hod*. In theory the different sides have truth; in doing it, one way is best, and even if it is not the best, doing it one way matters more than finding more possible ways.

So for a proactive, task-oriented person it matters less whether the system is the best. "It's better to have a system and a leader" and get things done than to sit working out the best system: in theory it can always be improved, and you never get anything done. That is why *Elul* is the time to stop and make a *cheshbon hanefesh* (an accounting of the soul); the rest of the year you focus on doing, without second-guessing yourself.

phrases.he: ודרך כלל, הרי רק מבחינת נה''י דאבא שמלובשים בנה''י דאימא, משם נמצא מקור המוחין לזעיר אנפין, שהן בחינת המדות שלמטה מן השכל (כמו שיתבאר)

blocks.text: Only the *Nehi* of *Abba* enclothed in the *Nehi* of *Ima* is the source of the *mochin* of *Zeir Anpin*, the *middos* below the intellect: once you have a *midda*, an intellect says how and when to have it. Day to day you do not think about the meaning of life and your goals; you set your priorities once, and from them what to like and what to hate. That is an *uvchein* (a conclusion), and your intellect is just how to react to what goes on around you.

blocks.title: The job and the family
blocks.text:
A person has *ahava rabba* (great love) in the *Chagas* of his will: he loves his family, so his intellect has him get a job to support them. On the job, the *Nehi* of the will goes into the *Nehi* of the intellect: he has to do the job well, not think of his family all day. That practical intellect becomes the *mochin* of the *middos*: happy at a profit, scared of a loss.

It comes from the *Nehi* of *Abba* going into the *Nehi* of *Ima*. A gut feeling for how to do things is the *Nehi* of *chachma*; in the *Nehi* of *Ima* he understands it a little and explains to himself when to have the *midda*. How the *middos* of *Zeir Anpin* are born from the intellect comes later.

sections.title: Two unions: for their own sake and for new mochin; Shabbos, the Shema and mesirus nefesh
sections.summary: *Abba* and *Ima* unite either in their inner side, for themselves, like a couple who simply enjoy each other, or in *Nehi* alone, to give new *mochin* to *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, like workers calling a manager. That is the difference between *Shabbos* and the week. In the *Shema*, *Havaya Elokeinu* is the inner union and *Havaya Echad* the union below it; it is reached by *mesirus nefesh*, as the ten martyrs raised *MaN* to the inner side of *Abba*.

phrases.he: וידוע פרטי עניני יחודים דאבא ואמא
phrases.en: Now we're going to explain the *pratei yichudim* of *Abba* and *Ima*,

blocks.text: **Now we're going to explain the pratei yichudim** (the particular unions) **of Abba and Ima**, which have three main levels: their *Chabad* is like *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov*, their *Chagas* like the inner side of the week, and their *Nehi* the regular week. The last two are the verdict and the sentence: is this good or bad, and what should you do about it.

phrases.he: בין כשהוא בבחינת הפנימית לצורך עצמן,
phrases.en: whether it's a *yichud* in the *pnimiyus* for themselves,

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת ג׳ ראשין שבהן
phrases.en: which is the *gimmel rishonos*, the *Chabad* or the *Keser*, *chachma*, *bina* of the *mochin*,

phrases.he: קודם שמתפשטים במדות עדיין כו',
phrases.en: before it goes into the *middos*,

phrases.he: ובין כשמתייחדים לצורך מוחין חדשים לזעיר אנפין ונוקבה,
phrases.en: whether getting together to make new *mochin* for the *middos*

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת נה''י לבד כו'
phrases.en: which is just the *Nehi*,

blocks.text: **Whether it's a yichud in the pnimiyus for themselves**, like *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov*, **which is the gimmel rishonos** (the first three), **the Chabad or the Keser, chachma, bina of the mochin, before it goes into the middos**: *chachma* and *bina* come together only to understand the idea, not yet to apply it. A father and mother are also husband and wife, with a relationship that precedes their being parents: spending time together, talking, going out to eat, for nothing outside the relationship.

blocks.title: Calling the manager
blocks.text: Or **whether getting together to make new mochin for the middos**, for *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*. The *middos* run on autopilot on their instructions, but when they hit a problem they need new *mochin*, so you call a manager: "the regular workers don't have brains, they just follow policy." The union that brings out new *mochin* for how the emotions, thought, speech and action should be *b'poel mamash* (in actual practice), **which is just the Nehi**, is the outer side of the union.

phrases.he: וזהו ההפרש בין שבת לחול כו'
phrases.en: this is the difference between *Shabbos* and *chol*.

blocks.text: **This is the difference between Shabbos and chol** (the weekday). On *Shabbos* you learn just to know G-d, Torah *lishma* (for its own sake). Learning *halacha l'maaseh* (law for practice) is not called *lishma*: knowing the *halachos* in order to act is a separate *mitzva* from learning Torah, which is knowing G-d's wisdom as an end in itself.

So too *hisbonenus* in *davenen* (prayer) is not meant to change your *middos*. It is appreciating G-dliness for its own sake, *avoda* of the mind, not for *birur* (refinement), not even of your mind: *lada'as Havaya levad*, just to know G-d. That is *Shabbos*. During the week the focus is refining your *middos*: learning *halacha l'maaseh*, and contemplating *Chassidus* to come out with something practical in *avoda*. These are the two unions of the mind: learning a thing for itself, or to apply it.

phrases.he: (ובקריאת שמע הכוונה ביהו״ה אלהינ״ו, היינו בפנימית דאבא ואמא,
שמשם יהו״ה אחד,
phrases.en: as a result of that, *Havaya Echad*,

phrases.he: יחוד דזעיר אנפין ונוקבא
phrases.en: which is the idea of the *yichud* of *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*.

phrases.he: כשבא להם בחינת תוספת מוחין חדשים
phrases.en: When they get this new *mochin*,

phrases.he: כדי שיוכלו להוליד כו'
phrases.en: so they can give birth.

blocks.text: In *Krias Shema*, *Havaya Elokeinu* is the inner side of *Abba*: *Havaya* is *chachma*, *Elokeinu* is *bina*, their inner union. Your *kavana* (intention) is that everything in the world reveals G-d, as an end in itself: He is our G-d, everything has a G-dly essence, and we are essentially connected to Him without having to do anything; we only reveal the connection. *Elokim* normally means nature and limitations, but here *Havaya*, higher than all limitations and above reason, chose that our nature should be connected to Him.

Just *Elokeinu* would mean we have to work to get it. *Chachma* is the thing as it is from the essence; *bina*, the way it is associated with something, as in a language. *Havaya* is the revelation of G-d, and *Elokeinu* means He made our nature a vessel to reveal Him, which we neither work for nor deserve; that too comes from *Havaya*. So the Jew's connection to G-d is unconditional, above reason, depending on nothing and a means to nothing: "The nature of a Jew is that he's G-dly, that's it."

In *Shema Yisroel Havaya Elokeinu* you realize that *Havaya*, higher than nature, is our G-d. Learning the *hishtalshelus* you really only see it in you, the way he explains it in you, not in the world. Once you find G-d in you, it tells you *Havaya Echad*: He is in everything else the same way, by extension. Once you know the *nimshal* (what an analogy stands for) in you, how the *hishtalshelus* works in you, you know how it works in everything. As the Arizal says, one who knows how to make *yichudim* can know whatever he wants to know.

So *Havaya Elokeinu* is the inner side of *Abba*: just appreciating, as an end in itself, that you are connected to G-d. **As a result of that, Havaya Echad, which is the idea of the yichud of Zeir Anpin and Nukva**: G-d is one with the world and controls everything, the *middos* coming into *Malchus*, *hashgacha pratis* (Divine providence over every detail). But first you realize that G-d creates the world and there is nothing else, so everything is His choice and reveals Him. That changes your *middos* and how you see the world run: if every moment is recreated by His choice, everything is *hashgacha pratis*, everything has a lesson, and nothing can stop you from doing what G-d wants.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 36 opens in the middle of line 31, which tape 35 began; this continues it.

blocks.text: That new *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* comes **when they get this new mochin**. Your *middos* are as they are, and the world seems limited (to make money you have to do it this way), because your *mochin* are messed up: you think *teva* (nature) is a set thing. Once you realize that G-d recreates the world every moment, you fear nothing but G-d and are not *nispa'el* (overawed); you see the world differently. **So they can give birth.**

phrases.he: והיינו במסירת נפש דקריאת שמע,
phrases.en: And this is accomplished in the *mesirus nefesh* of *Krias Shema*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בתורה ומצות בלא מסירת נפש
phrases.en: when a person does Torah and *mitzvos* without *mesirus nefesh*,

phrases.he: אין היחוד רק בחיצוניות דאבא ואמא בזעיר אנפין ונוקבה, כמו שכתוב במקום אחר

blocks.text: **And this is accomplished in the mesirus nefesh** (self-sacrifice) **of Krias Shema.** With *mesirus nefesh* a person reveals his essential connection to G-d, based on nothing, not for any particular of Torah and *mitzvos*, and he can apply it to change his *middos*.

That is *Rosh Hashana* and *Yom Kippur*, and then *Sukkos*. Their *teshuva* (return) reveals this *mesirus nefesh*, a connection to G-d higher than Torah and *mitzvos*: "you don't care about the Torah and *mitzvos*, you just care about G-d." Realizing that, you do Torah and *mitzvos* with *mesirus nefesh*, from the essential connection that is the whole reality of you and the world. Nothing can separate you from it, so nothing scares or overawes you, and then you do Torah and *mitzvos* properly.

blocks.title: A child cannot yet have children
blocks.text: You need a new worldview. Before, a false one trapped you, and that inhibition limited your *middos* and deeds and made you a *baal middos*. A child cannot have children until he gets *tosefes mochin* (added intellect), until he matures enough to have the *daas* for it. To give to someone outside himself, he has to be conscious of his essence and not worry that he will lose it.

That is the *mesirus nefesh* of *Krias Shema*. But **when a person does Torah and mitzvos without mesirus nefesh**, he does not reveal G-d's essence. In a way he is not really doing a *mitzva*, only its outer action, not from the inner side of the *mochin*. It is how he was trained: he still believes what he always did and serves himself, like a child who learns that the best chance of lollipops is to listen to his mommy and *tatty*. It is *mitzvas anashim melumada* (a commandment of men, learned by rote), within his nature, not really for G-d.

So it does not change him; he stays within his limitations. In return G-d does not do miracles or change nature for him, since he lives in the false reality of nature and believes in it. But one who realizes that the world is an arena for Torah and *mitzvos* that cannot stop him makes that his nature. A *shliach* (emissary) of the Rebbe who goes in the Rebbe's powers finds it normal that everything works out: "So then miracles happen all the time." It is *midda k'neged midda* (measure for measure).

phrases.he: וכמו בענין עשרה הרוגי מלוכה
phrases.en: like the ten martyrs

phrases.he: שהעלו מיין נוקבין לאבא ואמא בבחינת הפנימית על ידי מסירת נפש דוקא)
phrases.en: they made a *ha'ala'as MaN* to *pnimiyus* of *Abba*

blocks.text: **Like the ten martyrs**, whom we read about on *Yom Kippur*: through *mesirus nefesh* davka **they made a ha'ala'as MaN** (a raising of *mayin nukvin*, the receiver's arousal from below) **to pnimiyus of Abba** enough to sustain the worlds until *Moshiach*; G-d's pleasure in it made the whole thing worth doing just for them. *Mesirus nefesh* serves no purpose, not even Torah and *mitzvos*. It shows the essential connection, the *yechida* (the essence of the soul), and revealing that is the main thing of the world.

blocks.title: The interested students
blocks.text: It is like any relationship, a teacher and students, a husband and wife. If students put in effort and show big interest, that is a *ha'ala'as MaN*: you feel they really want it, and you want to give more. It works both ways: when a husband feels his wife is dedicated to him and appreciates him, he is motivated to give more and be more.

*Mesirus nefesh*, selfless dedication, reveals the essential connection, higher than anything: he gives himself over to you, as with *naaseh* before *nishma*. Our commitment is the *MaN* to G-d; His commitment to us is the drawing down of *MaD* (*mayin duchrin*, the giver's flow). There is commitment to the *mitzvos*, and *mesirus nefesh* to G-d, higher than the *mitzvos*. The martyrs gave their bodies and gained nothing; it was only to show they are for G-d, willing to die, even tortured to death, if He wants it.

blocks.title: The chassid willing to give his life
blocks.text: There is dedication to a subject, and dedication to you. A teacher gives far more when students will listen to whatever he says and give up everything for him. Imagine a *chassid* of the Rebbe willing to give his life away: that is a big *ha'ala'as MaN*.

blocks.title: The Holocaust and Moshiach's delay
blocks.text: The Holocaust was in a way even more: often they had no choice, and it was everybody. The story where they sing *Ani Maamin* is a crazy *ha'ala'as MaN*. He does not understand how such things can happen without *Moshiach* coming: it is so disproportionate, a huge, ridiculous *ha'ala'as MaN*, and what comes from it?

sections.title: Upper and lower Abba and Ima: Yisroel Saba and Tevuna, and the mazalos that give souls
sections.summary: The union of the upper *Abba* and *Ima* is the couple as husband and wife; the lower, *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna*, is them as father and mother, the intellect as it is revealed outward, felt in *Yisroel Saba* and explained in *Tevuna*. To give *mochin* to *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* for the birth of souls, the union must reach up to the two *mazalos* of *Arich*: a soul needs the essence of the intellect, not yet set in a form.

phrases.he: (וזהו ענין יחוד אבא ואמא עילאין ויחוד אבא ואמא תתאין,
phrases.en: and this is the idea of the upper union of *Abba* and *Ima*, and the lower union of *Abba* and *Ima*.

phrases.he: שהוא ישראל סבא ותבונה, כמו שכתוב למעלה בענין בינה ותבונה באריכות
ובחינת ישראל סבא הוא ו׳ קצוות דאבא ותבונה ו׳ קצוות דאימא

blocks.text: **This is the idea of the upper union of Abba and Ima, and the lower union of Abba and Ima.** The upper is *Abba* and *Ima*; the lower is *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna*, the six directions of *Abba* and of *Ima*, as was explained at length about *bina* and *tevuna*.

phrases.he: ויש עוד ישראל סבא למעלה גם מאבא ואמא עילאין
שהוא ו׳ קצוות דחכמה סתימאה דאריך אנפין
ותבונה ו׳ קצוות דבינה דאריך אנפין
שמשם נמשך שורש יחוד אבא ואמא עלאין בבחינת ג׳ ראשין שבהן כו')

blocks.text: There is also a *Yisroel Saba* above the upper *Abba* and *Ima*, the six directions of the hidden *chachma* of *Arich Anpin*, and a *Tevuna*, those of its *bina*. There is the root of the upper union, in the *gimmel reishin* (three heads), so *chachma* and *bina* can unite in their pure state, for their own revelation, not for the children. Father and mother as husband and wife are the upper union; as father and mother, the lower. In the *mashal*, *Abba* and *Ima* are the parents' personality, their *mochin* and *middos*; *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna* are like the reproductive organs: the *middos* of the *chachma* revealed outward.

The root of the upper union comes from that *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna* higher still, in *Arich*. A really smart person, who has the essence of the intellect, can explain it to a little kid; that comes soon. Chapter two explained *bina* and *tevuna*.

*Yisroel Saba* differs from *chachma* the same way: applied intellect against pure. *Tevuna* is the *middos* of *bina* revealed outward, what the intellect dictates about good, bad and how to act: like learning *Shulchan Aruch* as against *Gemara*, where even the *halacha* is hidden in the pure abstract thing, at least as we learn it. *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna* differ only in whether you can explain it. Rav, who knew the *halacha* and just felt it without being able to say why, is *Yisroel Saba*.

Normally pure intellect is higher than application. But there is a higher will, a higher level of application, in a way above pure intellect: the real thing of the Torah is doing the *mitzvos*, and its essence comes out when you apply it and experience it. That is what made you want to understand even its pure side, which is itself a *mitzva*; even the highest things should come out somehow as applied.

blocks.title: Parents and the will for children
blocks.text: Even not in a particular way, an attitude of wanting to be connected to G-d, *lishma*, is the spirit of the law, and it lets you get the letter right. So with parents: their essential relationship precedes the kids and is in a way higher, but they married mainly to make a family, and that will brought them together; they are not just friends. The strong, essential will for children makes the love between husband and wife so strong, since that love is not essential in itself, as between a father and son. It starts *talui b'davar* (dependent on a thing), and then is revealed as essential.
So the six directions of *Abba* are the intuitive halachic thing: you cannot explain it, but you have a *daas Torah* (a Torah sense), a *chush*, a feeling.

phrases.he: והנה כאשר נמשך מאבא ואמא מוחין לזעיר אנפין ונוקבה בשביל תולדות הנשמות,
phrases.en: when *Abba* is giving brains to *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* in order to give birth to souls,

phrases.he: צריך להיות היחוד באבא ואמא בפנימית המוחין, בשרשם בב' מזלות דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: then there has to go to the *pnimiyus* of *Abba*, all the way up to the two *mazalos*.

phrases.he: (והיינו בני כו' במזלא תליה כו')
phrases.en: To have children and also *chayei u'mezonei* depends on the *mazal*.

blocks.text: **When Abba is giving brains to Zeir Anpin and Nukva in order to give birth to souls**, the union must reach the inner *mochin*: **then there has to go to the pnimiyus of Abba, all the way up to the two mazalos**. As explained elsewhere, *banei, chayei u'mezonei b'mazla talya*: **to have children and also chayei u'mezonei** (life and sustenance) **depends on the mazal**.

For it to be a soul, a living thing that can change, you need the essence of the intellect. To *paskenen* (rule on) *halacha*, learning *halacha* and what the Gra says is not enough: you have to know *pnimiyus haTorah* (the inner Torah), *Abba* in its essence, the real goal, G-d and what He likes, the spirit of the law. "Just tell me what to do and I'll do it" is not good enough, because there will always be gray areas.

Otherwise it is not a soul but an angel, which does what it is told, like a machine, and cannot choose. To give birth to souls, with free choice and the ability to act creatively, the inner *mochin* have to be revealed: G-d puts in a *chelek* (portion) of His essence. A *neshama* (soul) comes from the inner side of *Abba*, the level of the *mazal*, not yet limited to a form that would set it one way. So souls reveal how G-d transcends every limitation, and have free choice; they are at the level of the essence.

blocks.title: The liquid over the brain, and stem cells
blocks.text: So with the physical making of a baby: some of the liquid over the brain, the hidden *mochin*, comes down, the essence of life before it takes a particular form, "kind of like things like stem cells": undefined, so they can turn into anything. To have a child you bring out what in you is the undefined essence of life, so it can be made into something new.

sections.title: Kel Elyon and the great sage who can teach a child: why souls are born from above the intellect
sections.summary: *Kel Elyon* is the inner light of *Abba* going up to the *mazal*; from there *yesod* gives good kindnesses and "acquires everything". The *mashal*: only a *chacham muflag* who knows an idea at its source can explain it to a little child or bring out a new idea from it. So too souls are born only from a union of *Abba* and *Ima* that reaches above the source of their intellect, to the *mazalos*; and that is why it is on the night of *Shabbos*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר
שזהו ענין אל עליון,
phrases.en: this idea of *Kel Elyon*, the upper force, the upper power.

phrases.he: עליית אור פנימית אבא כשמקבל ממזל ונוצר כו'
phrases.en: That is when the light of *Abba*, the *pnimiyus* light of *Abba*, receives from the *mazal v'notzer*.

blocks.text: This is *Kel Elyon*: **the upper force, the upper power**. *Kel* is a name of G-d and means power. *Kel* is the light of *chachma*, and *Kel Elyon* is the inner light of *Abba* rising to its source, receiving from the *mazal v'notzer*, from the *mocha stima'a*.

phrases.he: אז גומל חסדים טובים,
phrases.en: then it's able to give over good kindnesses,

phrases.he: בבחינת יסוד
phrases.en: in a way of *yesod*,

phrases.he: שנקרא קונה הכל,
phrases.en: which is called, acquires everything,

phrases.he: להוליד תולדות בזעיר אנפין ונוקבה
phrases.en: to give birth in *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*.

blocks.text: **Then it's able to give over good kindnesses, in a way of yesod** (the attribute of relationship), **which is called, acquires everything**, *koneh hakol*, **to give birth in Zeir Anpin and Nukva**. Feeling the real essence of the intellect, you aim at the truth, and what you do is really *tovim*: *tov* is actually helpful, while *chesed* is being nice, and you can mean well and not really help.

*Koneh hakol*: to acquire is to have something separate connected to you and revealing you; here, children, your essence passing into someone separate. For that you have to reach above how you are revealed consciously in your body, to a level of your soul that could have gone into another body, to other parents, made other choices, "and it would've been you, too." At that level anything can connect to it, so a child, really a separate person, can be called yours: there your essence *mamash* went into him.

phrases.he: וזהו וזוכר חסדי אבות ומביא גואל לבני בניהם כו'
phrases.en: And this is what it means that He remembers the kindness of the fathers and brings redemption to the children's children.

blocks.text: **And this is what it means that He remembers the kindness of the fathers and brings redemption to the children's children.** Going up to the source of the intellect, the source of the *avos* (fathers), He brings *geula* (redemption), the inner soul, to the children and their children. *Gevura* is how it comes out in the vessel, the *mochin*, limited and set; the *chasdei avos* (kindness of the fathers) is its connection to the source, unlimited, able to come out any way. Their children are the *middos*, their children's children the deed.

phrases.he: והמשל בזה ידוע,
phrases.en: the *mashal* of this is known,

phrases.he: כמו איש שהוא חכם מופלג ביותר,
phrases.en: a really, really, really smart guy.

phrases.he: כאשר יודע לעומק השכל ממקור חוצבו דוקא, אז יכול להיות משפיע לנמוך ביותר,
phrases.en: If you want to teach it to a really stupid, low person, you have to really understand it well and the real depth of the idea.

phrases.he: גם לתינוק קטן
phrases.en: then he can explain it even to a little kid,

phrases.he: לעשות צירופים חדשים באופן השכלת השכל ההוא, לא כהוויתו דוקא
phrases.en: Then he's able to explain it in a way that's totally different than the normal natural way that it's explained, which is very abstract and difficult, and he can explain it in a new way that the kid can understand.

phrases.he: וכן ביכולתו לחדש שכל אחר, להוליד מחדש מחמת זה השכל
phrases.en: He can also come up with new *sechel* from it,

blocks.text: **The mashal of this is known**: a *chacham muflag* (a wondrous sage), **a really, really, really smart guy**. **If you want to teach it to a really stupid, low person, you have to really understand it well**; **then he can explain it even to a little kid**, **in a way that's totally different than the normal natural way that it's explained, which is very abstract and difficult**. **He can also come up with new sechel from it**: he has the essence, not limited to its form.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן מי שאינו חכם מופלג
phrases.en: somebody that is not a wondrous *chacham*, he doesn't get the *etzem* of it that's higher than it,

phrases.he: ואינו תופס רק החכמה והשכל דברים כהוויתן לבד
phrases.en: He only understands it as it is, what was explained to him.

phrases.he: די להפקיע להשיגו לעצמו בלבד
phrases.en: So, for him, it's enough that he's able to understand it for himself,

phrases.he: אבל לא יוכל להוליד חדשות ממנו כלל
phrases.en: he's not able to get anything new from it,

phrases.he: וכל שכן שלא יוכל להוליד ולהשפיל הסבר השכל להבינו לתינוק כו'
phrases.en: For sure he can't explain to a child,

phrases.he: ונמצא שבחינת נה''י דחכמה, שהוא בחינת יסוד, הכח המשפיע למקבל,
phrases.en: so it comes out the *Nehi* of the *chachma*, which is the *yesod*, the power of being *mashpia*, of teacher, the ability to be a teacher to a student,

phrases.he: תלוי בכח המשכיל, מקור חוצב השכל
phrases.en: depends on the *koach hamaskil*, which is the source of the intellect,

phrases.he: מאין ליש דוקא כו'
phrases.en: which brings it from its abstract essence to like a tangible form,

blocks.text: Whereas **somebody that is not a wondrous chacham, he doesn't get the etzem** (essence) **of it that's higher than it**. **He only understands it as it is, what was explained to him**. **So, for him, it's enough that he's able to understand it for himself**, but **he's not able to get anything new from it**: he sees it only in its current form and cannot take the essence into other forms. **For sure he can't explain to a child**: he makes no *chiddush* even in the abstract, and a little child is totally irrelevant to him.

**So it comes out the Nehi of the chachma, which is the yesod, the power of being mashpia** (the giver), the ability to teach a student, **depends on the koach hamaskil** (the power of insight), **which is the source of the intellect**. There it is abstract and can come into any form, so one who taps into it can explain it even to a little kid.
So if you want to understand *Chassidus* well, the best thing is to teach it: "Just learning it, you're never going to understand it well, you have to teach it."

phrases.he: וכך הוא בענין תולדות הנשמות
phrases.en: same thing with this birth of souls,

phrases.he: מבחינת נה''י
שאינו מוליד כי אם בתוספת כח במקור המוחין שלו מלמעלה מעלה מן השכל כו'
phrases.en: In order for the souls to come out from the *mochin*, spiritually, it has to reveal the *etzem* that's higher than the *sechel*.

phrases.he: והוא הטעם שבשביל תולדות נשמות על ידי יחוד אבא ואמא,
צריך להיות מלמעלה ממקור המוחין דאבא ואמא
phrases.en: That's why it has to go higher than the source of the *mochin* of *Abba*,

phrases.he: שזהו מבחינת מזלות דחכמה סתימאה שהוא למעלה גם מחכמה ובינה דאריך אנפין עצמו כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: the *mazalos* are higher even than the *chachma* and *bina* of *Arich Anpin*, because the *mazalos* go all the way up to the *Keser*, all the way to the *etzem*.

blocks.text: **Same thing with this birth of souls**: **in order for the souls to come out from the mochin, spiritually, it has to reveal the etzem that's higher than the sechel**, so **it has to go higher than the source of the mochin of Abba**. And the other way around: for G-d to do miracles, to change things, we need *mesirus nefesh*. That is the *mazalos*, and **the mazalos are higher even than the chachma and bina of Arich Anpin, because the mazalos go all the way up to the Keser, all the way to the etzem**.

phrases.he: והיינו טעם ליחוד פנימית דאבא ואמא בליל שבת קודש
phrases.en: this is why the *pnimiyus yichud* of *Abba* is the night of *Shabbos Kodesh*,

phrases.he: מפני שהוא בשביל להוליד נשמות
phrases.en: because it's in order to bring down souls,

phrases.he: שלכך אז דוקא זמן זיווגא דחכימין
phrases.en: and that's why *talmidei chachamim*, their time when they have relations is *davka* on *Shabbos*,

phrases.he: שהן תלמידי חכמים שנקרא קודש,
phrases.en: because *talmidei chachamim* are called *kodesh*,

phrases.he: ושבת שרשו בקודש העליון,
phrases.en: and *Shabbos*, its source is in the *kodesh elyon*,

phrases.he: בחינת פנימית אור אבא כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין:
phrases.en: which is the *pnimiyus* of *Abba*, which receives from the *Keser*.

blocks.text: **This is why the pnimiyus yichud of Abba is the night of Shabbos Kodesh, because it's in order to bring down souls.** **And that's why talmidei chachamim** (Torah scholars), **their time when they have relations is davka on Shabbos**, *zivuga d'chakimin*: **because talmidei chachamim are called kodesh, and Shabbos, its source is in the kodesh elyon** (the higher holiness). They focus on the inner side of *Abba*, Torah *lishma* and the essential connection to G-d, so theirs is on *Shabbos*, its time.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does a person whose intellect receives from the *mazalos* become good at a thing, and what do the hockey cards show?
Why is *Shabbos* called *kodesh* and *oneg*, but *Yom Tov* only *mikra kodesh* and *simcha*?
What does *Drawing on the Right Side of the Brain* teach about the *koach MaH* of *chachma*, and how does naming reveal *Atik* in *bina*?
In what two ways is silence a fence for wisdom, and why does being quiet "get you double"?
How do *netzach* and *hod* of *Abba* hold up the intellect, and what do the lashes and the first offender show?
Why can only a *chacham muflag* explain an idea to a little child, and what does that show about the birth of souls?

Kiddush (32 w1279-1322): he says the mitzva d'oraisa is to enjoy, with wine, "I don't think that the mitzva though is to say the kiddush", then that one says it verbally to be mekadesh the day. The usual ruling (Rambam, Shabbos 29:1) is that the Torah commandment of kiddush is verbal. Also kept as said: "on Shabbos, if you don't enjoy wine, you're not supposed to have wine" (32 w1461-1478); also flagged, the publishable text drops that sentence.

The TV debate story (34 w552-807): he names "Rabbi Hollander, I think"; the identity is his recollection and is not checked. The publishable text drops the name and the remarks about the Reform rabbi and Reform Judaism.
